svg.title: Target steadiness versus response: four deterministic examples
svg.desc: Target decisions only, before motion feasibility. A threshold removes bounded noise, but delays slow drift and ignores small intended motion.
svg.text: Target selection only. No plant, robot, jerk, contact, or VLA performance model.
50 Hz proposals • alternating ±0.5 mm error • 2 mm strict gate • independently specified true target
Fixed hold: noise can be ignored
Gate target stays fixed. Filtering reduces noise, but its target still changes.
20 mm step: large changes pass the gate
Gate selects immediately; the selected target retains a 0.5 mm bias.
3 mm slow drift: commitment creates lag
Gate waits, jumps once, and ends 0.97 mm short of the true target.
1 mm intentional move: the gate misses it
A low-jitter score can hide task failure: the gate never selects this move.
The gate removes pure noise here. It does not prove physical steadiness or task completion.
This 50 Hz plot is one trace. At 100 and 200 Hz, dwell aliases exact alternation to a constant; see cadence sensitivity in results.json.
Hold-error windows, response criteria, exact checks, and full traces are in results.json. Reproduce with experiment.py.
